content.text:
I fixed it, and both programs from the issue now parse without errors.

**Cause:** in `parseFunctionBody` (`packages/babel-parser/src/parser/expression.js`), the parser starts a fresh expression scope for every function body. It only closed that scope when the body was a block (`{ ... }`). An arrow with an expression body, like `()=>null`, left its scope open. So after the arrow inside `f`'s default parameters, the stack still held `f`'s parameter scope. When the parser later reached `await` or `yield` in the outer function body, it thought it was still inside parameters and raised the error.

**Fix:** I moved `this.expressionScope.exit()` out of the block-body branch to the end of the function, so it runs for both kinds of body. That's the only change.

**Checks:** I rebuilt the parser and parsed the two programs from the issue, plus a similar async case (`async function g() { (x = () => 1) => 2; await 1; }`). All three parse cleanly. The full `packages/babel-parser` Jest suite passes (10,733 passed, 161 skipped). As asked, I didn't add any test fixtures.
